newsitem.title: HONG KONG: TVB optimistic about 1997 revenues.
newsitem.headline: TVB optimistic about 1997 revenues.

text.p: Television Broadcasts Ltd (TVB) said on Tuesday that it expected a pickup in revenues helped both by celebrations for Hongkong's handover to China and by better consumer confidence.
"Both those factors should help our turnover for this year," Alex Ying, TVB's general manager, corporate affairs told reporters after the group's annual meeting.

After more than 150 years of British rule, Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty on July 1, and a multi-million dollar extravaganza is planned, featuring fireworks, lasers, an illuminated barge fleet and giant balloons.
TVB, a television producer, broadcaster and cartoon distributor, planned to broadcast the handover live, TVB general manager Ken K.L. Lam said.
Lam said bookings for advertising airtime during the event had been "very good".
Asked about future prospects, Ying said TVB was developing new platforms to distribute Chinese programmes abroad.
"Since we are the largest producer of Chinese programmes all these new platforms obviously add on to our turnover and give us a greater reach into the world market," Ying said.
While growth in sales in China had been slow, TVB expected China to contribute a higher proportion of both profits and earnings to the group, Ying said.
"China, obviously, features prominently in our strategic plan," he said.
TVB executives declined to comment on the decision in February by Pearson Plc to sell a 10 percent stake in TVB to Shaw Brothers (Hong Kong) Ltd.
